entries.title: Depends who's asking
entries.body:
The beetle asked whether I could sting. I curled my abdomen a little higher.

"Depends who's asking."

He backed down the twig. I kept both forelegs raised until he was gone, which took longer than I would have liked. Then I ate the leaf beside me. A very good leaf. I had been looking at it throughout the confrontation.

He came back with someone else.

"That's her."

The second beetle kept a careful distance. Asked if I would deal with a spider.

I said I didn't work with spiders.

"Too dangerous?"

"Personal reasons."

They left me another leaf. I have put it beside the first one. I am beginning to see how this could get out of hand.

entries.body: I fell off the leaf and landed in the soil. Several things down here have no legs. I described the accident as a visit.

entries.title: Last bite
entries.body: I said I could stop whenever I wanted. Then I followed the edge round until I was hanging underneath it. Apparently I wanted to stop over here.

entries.title: Don't answer yet
entries.body:
She asked what I liked about her.

I had an answer. It was an excellent answer about the red of her back. Then I remembered that mine was red too, and that I had already spent most of the morning discussing it.

I lowered my head toward her. Tried to look as though I was considering the question deeply. The neck helped. It gives a simple hesitation somewhere to go.

"Take your time," she said.

This made it worse.

I could have mentioned her feet. I liked them. I liked how she put them exactly where she wanted to go, without any of this.

I told her that.

She waited.

"Without any of what?"

I raised my head again. We were going to need longer.

entries.title: An advance
entries.body: He asked if I wanted to get closer. I said I already had. He was measuring from my eyes.

entries.title: Before you go
entries.body:
Kit announced that he was old enough to go without a kiss. He had gone almost the width of my body when I called him back.

"Something on your face."

There wasn't. I kissed him. He endured it with his eyes open, looking past me at the grass.

Pip came up from the hole and asked what Kit had done. Nothing, I said. That was the problem. He hadn't done anything yet. All the things he might do were waiting out there and I wanted him to smell like home for a little longer.

Kit left again. I did not call him.

He came back on his own.

"You've got something on your face."

I held still. He picked off an actual seed and ate it.

Pip was watching. I kissed him instead.
